sanskrit: iyaṃ yā musalāhatā dṛṣatpiṣṭā viṣāsutā | tapur agnis tapur dyaus tapus tvaṃ sure bhava ||
english: This one that has been struck by the pestle, ground by the millstone, infused with poison — Agni burns, the sky burns; burn thou likewise, O surā.

sanskrit: viṣaṃ te tokma rohayanto 'bruvan viṣaṃ kumbhe 'va srava | viṣaṃ ta āmanaṃ sure viṣaṃ tvaṃ hasta āhitā viṣaṃ pratihitā bhava ||
english: Those who cause the sprout to grow declared thee poison; let the poison flow down into the jar. Thy raw state is poison, O surā; set in the hand thou art poison — become [thou] placed-back-as-poison.

sanskrit: siṃhas te astu taṇḍulo vyāghraḥ paryodanam | pṛdākūr astu nagnahur vṛkasya hṛdi saṃ srava ||
english: Let the grain be a lion for thee, the boiled rice a tiger; let the kneading-board be a spotted serpent — flow together [as if] into the heart of a wolf.

sanskrit: iyaṃ yā pātra āsūtā śaṣpasrakvā vighasvarī | varāhamanyur ajany uttānapādam ardaya ||
english: This one that has been fermented in the vessel, dripping with fresh grass, crackling with residue — born of the fury of a boar, crush the one who lies with feet upturned.

sanskrit: udardanī pracyavanī pāṃsupiṅgā vighasvarī | utkhātamanyur ajani yat paścāt tat puras kṛdhi ||
english: Swelling up, causing to fall, dust-tawny, crackling with residue — born of fury dug up from the ground: what is behind, make thou that to be in front.

sanskrit: viṣaṃ te pavane sure rudhiraṃ sthāle astu te | mathnantv anyo anyasmā iṣudhīṃs tvad dhanus tvat ||
english: Let thy straining be poison, O surā; let there be blood in thy vessel. Let them churn quivers and bows away from thee, one from another.

sanskrit: viṣapāvāno rudhirāś caranti pātāro martās tavase sura ime | hatāso anye yodhayanty anyāṃs tam ic chaṃsa mahimānaṃ surāyāḥ ||
english: These mortal drinkers walk about blood-smeared, drinking poison, made powerful by thee, O surā. Some, struck down, still incite others to fight — proclaim that very greatness of surā.

sanskrit: tān vīrudho visravo balena- -ut pātaya mādaya yodhanāyai | bhinnāratnīr bhinnaśīrṣṇā sam ṛcchatām ārtacelo visravan te surāpaḥ ||
english: Strike them down with force, O plant with running sap; intoxicate them for combat. Let the surā-drinker, with garments torn, with forearms broken, with head shattered, encounter [his fate] — running with thy stream.

sanskrit: viṣāsutāṃ pibata jarhṛṣāṇā asnā saṃsṛṣṭaṃ rudhireṇa miśrām | chinnahastaś carati grāme antar vairahatyāni bahudhā paṇāyan ||
english: Drink the poison-infused [brew] in great excitement, mixed with raw flesh, blended with blood. The one whose hand has been cut off wanders through the village, bartering manifold deeds of hostile slaying.

sanskrit: asimatīm iṣumatīm un nayāmi satād adhi | mādayābhi mādaya- -ahir ivainān pra ropaya- -anyo 'nyasya moc chiṣan ||
english: I lift up the sword-bearing, arrow-bearing [power] from the hundred. Intoxicate, thoroughly intoxicate them; cause them to rear up like a serpent; let them not leave one another.

sanskrit: anu te manyatām agnir varuṇas te 'nu manyatām | tatas te putro jāyatāṃ sa varmī goṣu yudhyatām ||
english: May Agni consent for thee; may Varuṇa consent for thee. From that let a son be born to thee; let him, clad in armor, fight among the cattle.

sanskrit: idaṃ vāyo 'nu jānīhi- -idam indra bṛhaspate | āñjanaṃ putravedanaṃ kṛṇmaḥ puṃsavanaṃ vayam ||
english: Know this, O Vāyu; know this, O Indra [and] Bṛhaspati. We perform this ointment-rite for the obtaining of a son, [this rite] that causes the birth of a male.

sanskrit: yenaitat pariṣṭabhitaṃ yasmāt putraṃ na vindase | indrāgnī tasmāt tvainasaḥ pari pātām ahardivi ||
english: That by which this [womb] has been obstructed, on account of which thou dost not obtain a son — from that sin may Indra and Agni protect thee day by day.

sanskrit: atharvāṇo aṅgiraso viśve devā ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | śṛṇvantv adya me havam asyai putrāya vettave ||
english: May the Atharvans, the Aṅgirasas, all the gods who strengthen cosmic order — may they hear my invocation today, for the obtaining of a son for her.

sanskrit: indrāṇī varuṇānī sinīvāly utāditiḥ | varutry ugrā patnīnāṃ putram adya dideṣṭu te ||
english: Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, Sinīvālī, and also Aditi — Varutrī, the fierce one among the consorts of the gods: let her point out a son for thee today.

sanskrit: putraṃ te mitrāvaruṇā putraṃ devī sarasvatī | putraṃ te aśvinobhā- -ā dhattāṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
english: May Mitra and Varuṇa place a son in thee; may the goddess Sarasvatī [grant] a son; may both Aśvins, garlanded with lotus, bestow a son upon thee.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ ca nāma jagrabha yeṣāṃ ca nopasasmara | devās te sarve saṃgatya putraṃ jaivātṛkaṃ dadan ||
english: Those whose names I have grasped and those whose names I have not remembered — all those gods, assembling together, shall grant thee a son full of vitality.

sanskrit: ātmana enaṃ nir mimīṣva sa tvat pari jāyatām | tvaṃ bījam urvareva tvaṃ bibhṛhi yonyām ||
english: Fashion him forth from thine own self; let him be born all around thee. Thou art the fertile field for the seed — do thou bear it in the womb.

sanskrit: pṛthivī saha yajñair nakṣatraiḥ saha sūryaḥ | vātaḥ patatribhiḥ saha putram adya dideṣṭu te ||
english: The earth together with the sacrifices, the sun together with the nakṣatras, the wind together with the birds — let them point out a son for thee today.

sanskrit: vṛṣā jajñe madhavāno 'yaṃ madhumatībhyaḥ | sa u te yonim ā śayāṃ baḍ dakṣaḥ puruṣo bhavan ||
english: This bull, Madhavāna, was born from the honey-rich [plants]; let him indeed lie down in thy womb — potent is [the power] becoming a male.

sanskrit: yoniṃ gaccha madhavāna yonyāṃ puruṣo bhava | tataḥ punar nir āyasi śīrṣṇā śroṇī vinonudat ||
english: Go to the womb, O Madhavāna; in the womb become a male. Thence thou comest forth again headfirst, pushing the hips apart.

sanskrit: bāṇavām̐ iṣudher iva kṛṇvan pitror yathā priyam | śroṇī ahiṃsann antarā daśame māsy āyasi ||
english: Doing as is pleasing to [thy] parents, as [an arrow] drawn from a quiver, not injuring the hips along the way, thou comest forth in the tenth month.

sanskrit: sa pratyaṅ pratyāvarttā- -ite saṃvatsare punaḥ | yathā jīvāsi bhadrayā bibharat tvā mahābhave ||
english: He turns back this way, comes back again at the [passing of the] year, so that thou mayest live by good fortune — bearing thee into great existence.

sanskrit: saṃ te yonim acīkl̥paṃ suprajāstvāya bhadrayā | tatrā siñcasva vṛṣṇyaṃ daśamāsyam avihrutam ||
english: I have made ready thy womb by good fortune, for the sake of fine progeny. There pour thou the virile, ten-months-destined [seed], unobstructed.

sanskrit: garbhas te yonim ā śayāṃ garbho jarāyv ā śayām | kumāra ulbam ā śayāṃ tvaṣṭrā kl̥pto yathāparu ||
english: Let the embryo lie in thy womb; let the embryo lie in the afterbirth. Let the boy lie in the amnion, fashioned by Tvaṣṭṛ joint by joint.

sanskrit: yathā rājan madhavāna tvaṃ bījaṃ virohasi | evā tvam asyā nir bhindhi kumāraṃ yonyā adhi ||
english: As thou, O king Madhavāna, causest the seed to sprout, so split forth the boy from her womb.

sanskrit: garbham adhān madhavāno garbhaṃ devo bṛhaspatiḥ | garbhaṃ ta indraś cāgniś ca garbhaṃ dhātā dadhātu te ||
english: Madhavāna has placed the embryo; the god Bṛhaspati has placed the embryo. May Indra and Agni place the embryo in thee; may Dhātṛ place the embryo in thee.
